sabina.json.title: Present Perfect

rule.formula: Subject + have/has + past participle (V3)
points: Use have with I, you, we, they; has with he, she, it.
Use it for experiences and for past actions whose result matters now.
Signal words: ever, never, already, yet, just, since, for, recently.
Example: The region has experienced three disasters in six weeks.

sabina.json.lead: Complete the sentences, then build your own with the present perfect.

sabina.json.title: Past Passive

rule.formula: Subject + was/were + past participle (V3) (+ by …)
points: Use the passive when the action matters more than who did it.
was with a singular subject, were with a plural subject.
Add by + agent only when it is useful: The town was destroyed by the flood.
Questions: Were the warning systems tested?

sabina.json.lead: Complete the sentences with the past passive, then build them word by word.

sabina.json.title: Present Perfect or Past Simple?

rule.formula: Finished time → Past Simple (V2) · Up to now → Present Perfect (have/has + V3)
points: Past simple with a finished time: last August, in 2023, when she was young.
Present perfect with time up to now: since, for, so far, recently, yet.
Passive forms follow the same rule: was destroyed / has been destroyed.

sabina.json.lead: Look for the time words, then choose the tense.

abay.json.title: Gerunds and Infinitives

rule.formula: Verb + V-ing  or  Verb + to + V1
points: Gerund (V-ing) after enjoy, avoid, suggest, mind, finish, keep, practise, recommend, and after prepositions: good at, interested in, looking forward to, be used to. Example: I enjoy reading books.
Infinitive (to + V1) after decide, hope, want, refuse, plan, manage, agree, promise, and after adjectives: important, happy, difficult, easy. Example: She decided to apply for the job.
Look at the word before the gap to choose.

abay.json.lead: Look at the verb before the gap: a gerund verb takes V-ing, an infinitive verb takes to + V1.

abay.json.title: Modal Verbs: Deduction and Obligation

rule.formula: Subject + modal + V1  ·  Subject + modal + have + V3 (past)
points: Sure: must be / must have + V3. She must be asleep. He must have missed the train.
Maybe: might, may, could (have + V3). They may have made a mistake.
Impossible: cannot be / cannot have + V3. He cannot have done it.
Obligation and advice: must, must not, should, ought to. You ought to read the article.

abay.json.lead: How certain is the speaker, or what is the obligation? Choose the modal, and use have + V3 for the past.

araylim_1.json.title: Present Simple

rule.formula: Subject + V1 (he/she/it + V-s/-es) · do/does not + V1 · Do/Does … + V1?
points: Use it for facts, habits and routines.
Add -s or -es for he, she, it: The brain processes information.
Negatives and questions use do/does and the base verb.

araylim_1.json.lead: Complete each sentence with the present simple.

araylim_1.json.title: Present Continuous

rule.formula: Subject + am/is/are + V-ing
points: Use it for actions happening now and temporary situations.
Signal words: now, right now, at the moment, look!, listen!

araylim_1.json.lead: Complete each sentence with the present continuous.

araylim_1.json.title: Past Simple

rule.formula: Subject + V2 · did not + V1 · Did … + V1?
points: Use it for finished actions in the past: last night, yesterday, in 2020.
Learn the irregular verbs: go → went, see → saw.

araylim_1.json.lead: Build each sentence with the past simple.

araylim_1.json.title: Past Continuous

rule.formula: Subject + was/were + V-ing
points: Use it for an action in progress at a past moment.
Often with when or while: I was sleeping when the phone rang.

araylim_1.json.lead: Build each sentence with the past continuous.

araylim_1.json.title: Present Perfect

rule.formula: Subject + have/has + past participle (V3)
points: Use it for experiences (ever, never) and results that matter now.
Signal words: since, for, yet, already, just.

araylim_1.json.lead: Complete each sentence with the present perfect.

araylim_2.json.title: Future Forms

rule.formula: will + V1 · am/is/are going to + V1 · Present Simple for timetables
points: will: decisions made now, promises and predictions.
going to: plans and intentions: I am going to buy a telescope.
Present simple for timetables: The shuttle leaves at 9 AM.

araylim_2.json.lead: Choose the future form that fits the meaning.

araylim_2.json.title: Modal Verbs

rule.formula: Subject + modal + V1
points: must: strong obligation. must not: it is not allowed.
have to / do not have to: necessary / not necessary.
can: ability or permission. should: advice.

araylim_2.json.lead: Choose the modal verb that fits the meaning.

araylim_2.json.title: Mixed Tenses Review

rule.formula: Present Continuous for arrangements · Present Perfect with since/for
points: Arrangements: I am seeing the doctor tomorrow.
Up to now: I have lived here since 2015.

araylim_2.json.lead: Look at the time words, then choose the tense.

araylim_3.json.title: Future Plans: Will, Going to, Present Continuous

rule.formula: Present Continuous · going to · will
points: Present continuous: fixed arrangements. I am meeting the investors tomorrow.
Going to: plans, and predictions from evidence. Look at those clouds! It is going to rain.
Will: decisions made now, promises, predictions without evidence.

araylim_3.json.lead: Choose the future form from the context.

araylim_3.json.title: Future Continuous and Future Perfect

rule.formula: will be + V-ing · will have + V3 · When/If + present simple
points: Future continuous: in the middle of an action at a future time. This time tomorrow, I will be presenting.
Future perfect: finished before a future time, often with by. By 2030, AI will have taken over many tasks.
After when and if, use the present simple: If it rains, we will not go.

araylim_3.json.lead: Watch for by …, this time tomorrow, and when/if clauses.

araylim_3.json.title: Mixed Future Forms

rule.formula: Arrangement · Plan · Timetable · Prediction
points: Choose the form from the meaning, not from one signal word.
Timetables use the present simple: When does the movie start?

araylim_3.json.lead: Complete the sentences with the correct future form.

george.json.title: Present Simple and Present Continuous

rule.formula: Present Simple (V1 / V-s) · Present Continuous (am/is/are + V-ing)
points: Present simple: routines and facts. He trains every day.
Present continuous: happening now. Listen! Someone is knocking.
Signal words: every day, usually · now, look!, listen!

george.json.lead: Routine or right now? Choose the present tense.
